 My main model is something that I've ran for four years and I'll explain why right now. You either model something on pure mathematical rigor like z-scoring, order-flowing balances or you can model economic principles. Now building on top of mathematical rigor would often be a mean-referting system, an arbitrage system, etc. etc. When you start doing something like swing trading, value investing, you have to build on economic principles. Obviously there is differences in this. A mathematical misprising, an arbitrage opportunity is something that can decay much quicker. But something that is based on economic principles is something that has been recorded in the bit of a softer science called economics and has likely been recorded for 200 years. So if you record these principles in code, they will last you longer and they are more robust. So when I tell you that I base my model of triple momentum, which is not much more than a percentage difference of different periods, like 3, 6 and 12 months, which you believe me that I modeled that and it has been robust for four years. Hard to believe what it's true because it's based on those economic principles.
